roots.name: Transformation Narrative
roots.mechanism: Before/after identity shift — shows the person's life transformation after taking the course or joining the program
roots.why_it_works: Aspirational identification — the viewer sees themselves in the 'before' and wants the 'after'. Works especially well for housewives and job-holders who dream of a different life.
roots.visual_motif: Split-screen or side-by-side: left = old life (dull colors, stressed, office/kitchen), right = new life (bright, confident, laptop/phone, earning). Sometimes a single person shown in two contexts.
roots.compliance_notes: Must use real stories, not fabricated. Income figures need 'results may vary' disclaimer. Cannot guarantee the transformation.

competitor_examples.note: From Corporate Life → To Fitness Coach Life — split image, two versions of the same woman

roots.name: Income Proof / Screenshot
roots.mechanism: Social proof through visible earnings — payment screenshots, bank notifications, commission dashboards showing real numbers
roots.why_it_works: Nothing convinces like seeing real money. Addresses the 'is this real or scam?' objection head-on. The specific numbers make it feel tangible and achievable.
roots.visual_motif: Phone screen showing payment notification / bank credit / affiliate dashboard with earnings. Sometimes blurred partially for 'privacy'. Often held in hand or overlaid on a lifestyle photo.
roots.compliance_notes: Screenshots MUST be genuine. Must add disclaimer: 'Individual results may vary'. Cannot imply everyone earns this amount. Avoid showing unrealistic figures.

roots.name: Certification + Career Badge
roots.mechanism: Authority and credibility through visible certification — government logo, certificate mockup, recognized body name
roots.why_it_works: Indian audience deeply values certificates and official recognition. A 'government certified' course feels safer than a random online course. Answers 'is this legit?' instantly.
roots.visual_motif: Certificate mockup prominently displayed, often with government/NSDC logo, gold border, person's name filled in. Sometimes shown being held by a smiling graduate.
roots.compliance_notes: Must name the SPECIFIC certifying body — 'government certified' alone is too vague and potentially misleading. The certification must be real and verifiable.

roots.name: Problem-Agitation-Escape
roots.mechanism: Names the viewer's current pain (low salary, boring job, no independence, financial stress) then presents the course/program as the escape route
roots.why_it_works: Hits the emotional nerve first. The viewer feels 'that's me' before the solution appears. Works across all demographics — students (no job), housewives (no income), job-holders (stuck).
roots.visual_motif: Dark/frustrated imagery at top transitioning to bright/hopeful at bottom. Often uses text-heavy design with the problem in large font and solution below. Sometimes a person looking stressed then looking up.
roots.compliance_notes: Fine as long as the 'escape' doesn't promise guaranteed income or guaranteed job. Keep it about skills and opportunity, not certainty.

roots.name: Social Proof Counter
roots.mechanism: Large numbers of existing students / success stories / ratings create herd-following behavior
roots.why_it_works: If 5000+ people already did it, it must be safe. Reduces risk perception. The specific number (not 'many students') makes it concrete.
roots.visual_motif: Prominent counter number (5000+, 10,000+, 4.8★), often with student faces / grid of small photos / testimonial cards arranged around it.
roots.compliance_notes: Numbers must be real and verifiable. 'X students enrolled' is different from 'X students earning' — the latter needs proof.

roots.name: Urgency / Scarcity / Batch Closing
roots.mechanism: Limited seats, next batch starting soon, offer expiring — creates fear of missing out
roots.why_it_works: Converts fence-sitters. Indian audience responds strongly to 'last date' and 'limited seats' — educational context makes it feel more legitimate than ecommerce scarcity.
roots.visual_motif: Countdown timer, 'Only X seats left' badge, 'Batch starts [date]' banner. Often red/orange accent colors for urgency. Sometimes a calendar or clock icon.
roots.compliance_notes: Must be GENUINELY true. Perpetual 'last 5 seats' or evergreen 'offer ends today' is deceptive advertising under Consumer Protection Act 2019.

roots.name: Mentor / Authority Face
roots.mechanism: A credible mentor/founder speaking directly to camera, sharing their expertise and inviting the viewer to learn from them
roots.why_it_works: Personal trust — 'I'm learning from THIS person, not a faceless company'. Works especially well in Indian culture where guru/teacher relationship is valued. The face becomes the brand.
roots.visual_motif: Person speaking to camera or posed professionally. Often in a studio/office setting. Name + credentials displayed. Sometimes with a subtle background of their achievements (books, awards, screen).
roots.compliance_notes: The mentor must be real. Credentials must be genuine. Cannot make income promises through the mentor's voice.

roots.name: Comparison / VS Old Way
roots.mechanism: Degree vs digital skills, 9-to-5 job vs freelancing, traditional learning vs online learning — frames the old way as inferior
roots.why_it_works: Creates a clear 'aha' moment. The viewer instantly sees why the new option is better. Works well for people already frustrated with the traditional path.
roots.visual_motif: Two-column or VS split: left = old way (degree scroll, office cubicle, ₹15K salary), right = new way (laptop, freedom, earning potential). Often with ✗ and ✓ marks.
roots.compliance_notes: Fine as long as it doesn't disparage specific institutions by name or guarantee the 'new way' outcome. Compare the MODEL, not specific competitors.
